episodes.title: Race Conditions
episodes.summary: You typed "laptop", but the screen shows results for "la": makeup instead of laptops. Responses can come back out of order, and an old one overwrites the new one. Cancel stale requests with AbortController, and debounce the input.

challenges.text: Change the debounce to 150 ms, then to 800 ms. What changes for a fast typist, and for a slow one?
Move the AbortController and debounce logic into a reusable custom hook, useSearch(query), that returns { results, resultsFor, loading, error }.
Replace the AbortController with an "ignore" flag in the cleanup. Watch the timeline: which requests still run, and why is that worse?

episodes.interviewQuestion: A user types "laptop" in a search box, but the screen shows results for "la". Why does that happen, and how would you fix it?

episodes.title: Index as Key Bug
episodes.summary: You typed a note on one product, deleted the row above it, and the note jumped to a different product. React matched the rows by position, because the key was the index. Watch what React does to the DOM with key={index}, key={product.id} and key={Math.random()}.

challenges.text: With key={index}, add a product at the END of the list (not on top) and type notes. Why does the bug not appear? When is an index key actually fine?
The products lose their ids: map them to { title, price } only. Build a key without an id that still survives sorting and deleting, then explain why Math.random() and index both fail that test.
Add a <ProductForm key={selected.id}> editor under the list that resets when you pick another product, without any useEffect. Then remove the key and watch the form go stale.

episodes.interviewQuestion: A list of products has an input in every row. The user types in the first row and deletes that product, but the text stays in the first row, now under a different product. Why, and how would you fix it?

episodes.title: You Might Not Need an Effect
Loaders vs useEffect
episodes.summary: Fetching in useEffect starts the request only after the first render, so nested components fetch one after another. A React Router loader fetches before render, in parallel.

challenges.text: Set Network to "Slow" and open the same product in both modes. Which one feels better to use, and why?
Add a third request, "related products", as another nested route with its own loader. The total time should stay the same with loaders. Then try it in the useEffect version.
Make the reviews non-blocking: return their promise from the loader without awaiting it, and render it with <Suspense> and <Await>. The product should appear first.

episodes.interviewQuestion: How do you load the data a page needs in React? Would you fetch it in useEffect?

episodes.title: React 19 Actions
episodes.summary: Post a review the React 18 way: four useStates, a try/catch/finally, and a button that posts twice when you double click. Then let React 19 run the submit as an Action: pending, errors and the form reset are handled for you, and useOptimistic shows the review before the server answers.

challenges.text: In the Trap version, fix the double submit and the stale error with the least code you can. Count the lines you added, then compare with the Pattern version.
Add a "Clear" button inside the Pattern form that is disabled while the review is posting, using useFormStatus and no props.
Add a star rating summary above the reviews that updates optimistically in the Bonus version, and rolls back on its own when a review is rejected.

episodes.interviewQuestion: What are Actions in React 19, and what do useActionState and useFormStatus give you over a classic onSubmit handler?

episodes.title: Trigger → Render → Commit
episodes.pattern: Render is a function call; commit is the DOM
episodes.summary: Everyone says "React re-renders"… but what actually happens between typing a letter and your screen updating? A keystroke, a click, a server reply and a timer all go through the same three steps. Fire each one and watch which components React calls, and what really changes on the page.

challenges.text: Press "Server reply". It calls two setters, setTickets and setSyncedAgo, yet the render lane shows one pass. Explain why, then make it render twice on purpose and say what that costs.
Move the selected filter out of App and into the components that need it so that clicking Open no longer renders Header. Count the renders before and after, and explain what you traded.
Add a component that writes to document.title during render. Turn on StrictMode, watch it misbehave, then move the write to the right place and explain why render must stay pure.

episodes.interviewQuestion: What happens in React between a user clicking a button that calls setState and the screen updating?
